page: Vultr vhf-12c-48gb is a virtual server belonging to the High Frequency Compute family, built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 12 shared vCPUs mapped to 6 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with the instance, consisting of a 768 GB NVMe SSD. The CPU includes an L3 cache of 16 MB and supports hardware-level instructions such as AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard compute workloads, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1816.0 and a multi-core score of 7623.0. The server excels in single-threaded gzip compression, placing in the top tier with 41.11 GB/sec, and demonstrates strong text processing capabilities. However, memory performance presents a clear tradeoff: while small-block cached read bandwidth is average at 865.54 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the bottom 25% at 33.97 GB/sec and 18.41 GB/sec respectively. LLM inference performance is similarly constrained, with medium 7B models executing at a weak 6.46 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the vhf-12c-48gb offers a high density of NVMe storage and balanced memory-to-core resources on a shared CPU model, making it a viable option for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU execution. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, software compilation, and database operations that benefit from local NVMe speeds but can tolerate shared CPU scheduling.
